title: Virata: the year in disguise
hook: Prince Uttara boasts he'd beat the Kuru army if only he had a charioteer, and the dance teacher volunteers

segments.voice: Yesterday Draupadi woke the cook at night, and the dancing hall became a trap for Kichaka. Your line was the disguise bends, and it holds. Did you listen to someone all the way to the end? Day eight hundred eleven.
screen: `VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.` · `A NIGHT IN THE DANCING HALL.`

segments.voice: Cattle raiders. The Kauravas have heard that Kichaka is dead, and they come for King Virata's herds. The king has already ridden out to fight raiders on another side, taking Kanka, the cook and the herdsmen with him. At home, among the women of the palace, sits his young son, Prince Uttara. And Uttara talks big. If I only had a charioteer, he says, I'd beat the whole Kuru army. They'd look at me and wonder if I was Arjuna himself. The person he's talking about is standing a few feet away, in bangles. Today, a frightened prince, a dance teacher, and a ride back to the shami tree.
screen: `THE KAURAVAS RAID THE HERDS.` → `UTTARA'S BOAST.` → `ARJUNA IS IN THE ROOM.`

segments.voice: Sairandhri speaks up. Brihannala, she says, once drove a chariot for Arjuna. Uttara is embarrassed to take a dance teacher to war, but he has no one else. The teacher fumbles with the armor on purpose, putting it on wrong, and the palace women laugh. The princesses ask for fine cloths from the beaten Kurus for their dolls. Then the chariot rolls out, and Uttara sees the army: the banners, the elephants, the great warriors of the Kuru house, Bhishma, Drona, Karna. His boast falls apart. He jumps from the chariot and runs. And Brihannala runs after him. Long braid flying, robes swirling, across the field, and some of the Kuru soldiers watching think: that runs like a man, that runs like Arjuna. The teacher catches the prince, not to shame him, but to steady him. Don't be afraid, he says, in effect. You drive. I'll fight. Then they turn the chariot to the shami tree by the cremation ground. Uttara climbs up, unwraps the bundle, and finds weapons no dance teacher should own, the great bow Gandiva among them. Whose are these? he asks. And Brihannala tells him the truth. I am Arjuna. Notice who hears it first. Not a king, not an enemy. A scared boy who just ran away, and who is now trusted to hold the reins.
screen: `UTTARA'S BOAST` · `THE PRINCE RUNS` · `BRIHANNALA RUNS AFTER HIM` · then, large: `I AM ARJUNA`

segments.voice: Settle in and feel your feet on the floor. Bring to mind one thing you've been running from, small or large. Don't try to fix it. Breathing in, just turn toward it, the way Uttara had to turn the chariot around. Breathing out, hear the teacher's words to the prince: you drive. Let your hands rest as if they held the reins. Stay with the breath, facing it. If you pray, you can bring it into your prayer. The bell holds the time.
Virata. The kingdom whose frightened prince learns, on a battlefield, who his dance teacher really is.
Your line: I am Arjuna. Today, if someone near you panics, run after them, not away. Steady them, and give them something to hold. Day eight hundred eleven.

screen: `DAY 811 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: VIRATA: THE YEAR IN DISGUISE.`

howItsDone: Retellings of the Virata book linger on Uttara's boast and flight and on Brihannala chasing him across the field, a scene that mixes comedy with the moment Arjuna is revealed.

match.prompt: the cattle raid — tap the pairs.
pairs: said Brihannala once drove for Arjuna
asked for cloths for their dolls

myth: Uttara rode out bravely and never wavered
he saw the Kuru army, jumped from the chariot, and ran.
Brihannala ran after the prince across the field
braid flying, and some Kuru soldiers thought the runner moved like Arjuna.
Arjuna first revealed himself to King Virata
he told Prince Uttara, at the shami tree, before anyone else.

fork.setup: you're Brihannala. the prince you're driving has jumped from the chariot and is running away from the Kuru army. what do you do?
options: let him go and face the army alone.
run after him, bring him back, and let him drive while you fight.
throw off the disguise and call to the Kurus.
fork.reveal: Arjuna chases him down, steadies him, makes him the charioteer, and reveals himself to the boy at the shami tree.

trapdoor: what you thought: Uttara is just the comic coward of the story.
what it means: the frightened prince becomes the first to hear Arjuna's name, and the one trusted with the reins.
what a scholar hears: the hero's mask comes off for a scared boy, not a king, which turns the reveal into an act of care.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Virata Parva (Go-harana), the Kuru cattle raid, Uttara's boast and flight, Brihannala as charioteer, and the weapons recovered from the shami tree

notes: Audit: read against the Virata/Udyoga sequence in Ganguli as summarized; no factual, framing or repetition problem found; no change.

All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Virata is away fighting the Trigartas with four of the Pandavas when the Kurus raid from the other side; Uttara's boast in the women's quarters; Sairandhri's suggestion that Brihannala was Arjuna's charioteer.
Confirm Brihannala's deliberate fumbling with armor, the princesses' request for cloths for their dolls, and Kuru soldiers remarking that the runner resembles Arjuna.
